items.longBusinessSummary: Reddit, Inc. operates a digital community in the United States and internationally. The company's platform enables user to engage in conversations, explore passions, research new hobbies, exchange goods and services, create new communities and experiences, share laughs, and find belonging. It also organizes communities based on specific interests that enable users to engage in conversations by sharing experiences, submitting links, uploading images and videos, and replying to one another. Reddit, Inc. was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in San Francisco, California.

Title: Reddit vs. Snap: Which Social Media Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Author: Robert Izquierdo, The Motley Fool   Tue, October 27, 2026 at 7:28 AM GMT+1 6 min read
Published: 2026-10-27T06:28:39+00:00
=== BODY ===
As digital communities and visual communication evolve, investors are weighing the merits of different social platforms. Should you put your capital behind Reddit (NYSE:RDDT) or Snap (NYSE:SNAP) in 2026?
In its 2025 fiscal year (FY), revenue reached $2.2 billion, representing a year-over-year increase of 69.4%. The company reported net income of $529.7 million during this period. This resulted in a net margin of 24.1%, which is a significant improvement over the net loss reported in the prior fiscal year. High growth and positive earnings suggest the platform is successfully scaling its ad business.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the company carried a debt-to-equity ratio of zero, indicating it has no total debt relative to its shareholder equity. Its current ratio, which measures the ability to pay short-term obligations with current assets, was 11.6x. Free cash flow for the year was $684.2 million. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) represented 49.7% of operating cash flow, which inflates reported cash generation since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.
In FY 2025, revenue reached $5.9 billion, a growth rate of 10.6% compared to the previous year. Despite the revenue growth, the company reported a net loss of $460.5 million. This resulted in a net margin of negative 7.8%. While the net margin has improved from the previous year, the company continues to focus on reaching consistent net profitability as it scales its global user base.
As of its December 2025 balance sheet, Snap had a debt-to-equity ratio of 2.1x, meaning its total liabilities exceed shareholder equity. The current ratio stood at 3.6x, suggesting a healthy liquidity position for near-term needs. Free cash flow for the period was $437.2 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented 155% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.
Reddit faces risks related to user base concentration and the necessity of maintaining high engagement levels to attract advertisers. Competition for user attention is intense, coming from large platforms like Alphabet, Meta Platforms, and TikTok. Furthermore, the company relies on volunteer moderators, and any inconsistencies in content moderation could lead to advertiser churn or reputational damage. The platform is also subject to evolving global regulations and ongoing securities litigation.
Reddit carries a higher sales multiple reflecting its faster growth and positive net margin, while Snap appears cheaper on a revenue basis but carries higher debt.
Valuation metrics include sourcing from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from other data providers.
The P/S ratio measures the market value of the company against its sales over the past twelve months. The Forward P/E ratio compares the current share price to future earnings estimates over the next year.
I would invest in Reddit over Snap. In fact, I bought shares in Reddit while I sold my Snap holdings. Snap is cheaper from a valuation perspective, but that's because it has yet to make a profit, and its revenue growth is far below Reddit's.
Snap grew second-quarter sales by a solid 19% year over year to $1.3 billion, but it saw a year-over-year decline in average daily active users in North America, its largest market. This is not an encouraging sign, as it could signal waning interest in Snap's offerings.
Reddit continues to experience strong revenue expansion. Its Q2 sales of $805 million represented a 61% year-over-year increase, and the eighth consecutive quarter of over 60% growth. The trend demonstrates the company's ability to successfully generate sales from its daily active users, which increased 18% year over year in Q2.
Reddit's ability to continue growing its audience while remaining profitable, with a 183% year-over-year increase in Q2 net income, demonstrates it's a well-run company. That's why I chose to buy shares in this social media giant.
